push_1.title: First Push-Up
push_1.description: Achieve your first clean push-up: straight body line, chest touching the floor, full arm extension.

push_2.title: Push-Up Strength
push_2.description: Double your push-up capacity and tighten your form — consistent sets unlock the overhead and planche paths.

push_3.title: Diamond Push-Up
push_3.description: Hands form a diamond under the chest, elbows track behind — isolates the triceps and inner chest for elite pressing density.

push_4.title: Archer Push-Up
push_4.description: One arm bends while the other extends wide — asymmetric drill that builds unilateral pressing strength toward one-arm work.

push_5.title: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
push_5.description: Hands rotated out by your hips, body leaning forward — simulates planche loading on the wrists and shoulders while pressing.

push_oh_1.title: Pike Push-Up
push_oh_1.description: Hips high, hands shoulder-width — lower your head between your hands and press back up. Shifts load onto the shoulders, bridging the gap toward overhead pressing.

push_oh_2.title: Elevated Pike Push-Up
push_oh_2.description: Feet on a box or bench — the elevated angle increases shoulder range of motion and load, the direct step toward the handstand push-up.

push_oh_3.title: Wall Handstand Push-Up
push_oh_3.description: Kick up against the wall and press your full bodyweight overhead — the most direct loading pattern for handstand push-up strength.

push_oh_4.title: Handstand
push_oh_4.description: Balance on your hands away from the wall — controlled inversion demanding shoulder strength, wrist flexibility and spatial awareness.

push_oh_5.title: Handstand Push-Up
push_oh_5.description: Press from the floor to full lockout while inverted — the pinnacle of calisthenics overhead pressing strength.

push_pp_1.title: Planche Lean
push_pp_1.description: Lean forward over your wrists in a push-up position with hands rotated out — conditions the wrists and anterior shoulder for planche loading.

push_pp_2.title: Tuck Planche
push_pp_2.description: Lift both feet off the ground while leaning over your wrists with knees tucked — the first true planche position.

push_pp_3.title: Straddle Planche
push_pp_3.description: Legs extended wide in a straddle while holding the planche position — dramatically harder than the tuck, demanding total-body tension.

push_pp_4.title: Full Planche
push_pp_4.description: Body perfectly horizontal, legs together and locked — the legendary pinnacle of calisthenics pressing strength.

pull_1.title: First Pull-Up
pull_1.description: Achieve your first clean, full-range pull-up from a dead hang.

pull_2.title: Pull-Up Consistency
pull_2.description: Develop reliable pull-up strength across multiple reps. Unlocks the Front Lever path.

pull_3.title: Negative Pull-Ups
pull_3.description: Start from chin-over-bar and lower yourself as slowly as possible. This eccentric-focused variation builds the explosive pulling power needed for the Muscle-Up path.

pull_fl_1.title: Tuck Front Lever
pull_fl_1.description: Hang from the bar, tuck your knees to your chest and hold your body horizontal. Builds the scapular depression and lat strength needed for the full lever.

pull_fl_2.title: Straddle Front Lever
pull_fl_2.description: Extend your legs out in a wide straddle and hold horizontal. Dramatically harder than the tuck — demands total-body tension.

pull_fl_3.title: Full Front Lever
pull_fl_3.description: Body perfectly horizontal, arms straight, legs locked together — one of calisthenics' most coveted static holds.

pull_mu_1.title: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
pull_mu_1.description: Explode past chin-over-bar — drive until your chest touches the bar. Demands far more pulling power than a standard pull-up.

pull_mu_2.title: Kipping Muscle-Up
pull_mu_2.description: Use a controlled hip kip to generate momentum through the bar transition. Master the timing before eliminating the kip.

pull_mu_3.title: Strict Muscle-Up
pull_mu_3.description: Zero swing, zero kip — pull through and press above the bar with pure upper-body strength. The gold standard of pulling power.

pull_am_1.title: Archer Pull-Up
pull_am_1.description: One arm pulls while the other extends straight — a brutally asymmetric drill that develops unilateral lat strength toward the one-arm pull-up.

pull_am_2.title: Typewriter Pull-Up
pull_am_2.description: Pull to the bar then slide laterally from hand to hand at the top — an extraordinary display of horizontal pulling strength and control.

pull_oah_1.title: One-Arm Active Hang
pull_oah_1.description: Hang from the bar with a single arm, shoulder actively packed and depressed. Builds unilateral shoulder stability, grip endurance, and lateral chain strength.

pull_oapu_1.title: One-Arm Pull-Up
pull_oapu_1.description: The ultimate test of unilateral pulling strength — a full pull-up performed with a single arm, no assistance, no momentum. One of the rarest feats in all of calisthenics.

pull_rings_1.title: Ring Support Hold
pull_rings_1.description: Hold an active support on the rings — arms extended, body upright. This foundational position demands wrist, elbow and shoulder stability before any ring pulling work.

pull_rings_2.title: Ring Pull-Up
pull_rings_2.description: Full pull-ups on gymnastic rings demand grip stability and shoulder control that no fixed bar can replicate. The instability makes every rep harder.

pull_rings_3.title: Ring Muscle-Up
pull_rings_3.description: The pinnacle of ring pulling: a strict muscle-up on gymnastic rings demands elite transition power, shoulder stability, and wrist control under instability.

pull_weighted_1.title: Weighted Pull-Up
pull_weighted_1.description: Add a vest or belt and perform strict pull-ups under load. Starting at 10–20% bodyweight, the added resistance accelerates strength gains beyond pure bodyweight training.

pull_weighted_2.title: Weighted Pull-Up Volume
pull_weighted_2.description: Sustain high-rep weighted pull-up sets. Volume under load builds the raw pulling strength needed for the weighted muscle-up and heavier loading.

pull_weighted_3.title: Weighted Muscle-Up
pull_weighted_3.description: A muscle-up with added load — one of the most powerful feats in calisthenics. Demands explosive pulling, precise transition timing, and total-body tension.

core_1.title: Plank Foundation
core_1.description: Hold a perfect plank — body straight from head to heels, glutes and abs braced. The universal starting point for all core work.

core_2.title: Side Plank
core_2.description: Prop on one forearm and lift your hips — creates lateral core stiffness that transfers directly into human flag and hanging leg work.

core_hh_1.title: Dead Bug
core_hh_1.description: Lie on your back with arms and legs raised — lower opposite arm and leg while bracing. The foundational anti-extension core drill.

core_hh_2.title: Back Extensions
core_hh_2.description: Lie face-down and raise your chest and legs off the floor (Superman). Builds the posterior chain strength that balances hollow body work.

core_hh_3.title: Hollow Body Hold
core_hh_3.description: Lie on your back and brace into a hollow curve — shoulders off the floor, straight legs raised low. The fundamental full-body tension skill underpinning every calisthenics movement.

core_hh_4.title: Dragon Flag Negative
core_hh_4.description: Lie on a bench, grip behind your head, and lower your body slowly from vertical to horizontal. The eccentric loading phase that prepares you for the full dragon flag.

core_hh_5.title: Dragon Flag
core_hh_5.description: Grip behind your head and hold or lower your body perfectly horizontal — only your shoulders touch the bench. Total anti-extension strength at its peak.

core_bb_1.title: Active Hang
core_bb_1.description: Hang from the bar with shoulders actively depressed and packed — the foundation of all bar-based core and pulling work.

core_bb_2.title: Hanging Knee Tucks
core_bb_2.description: Hang from the bar and drive your knees to your chest. Builds the hip-flexor compression and shoulder stability needed for harder hanging core work.

core_bb_3.title: Hanging Leg Raises
core_bb_3.description: Hang from the bar and raise straight legs to horizontal — demands serious hip-flexor strength, grip endurance and full spinal control.

core_bb_4.title: Toes to Bar
core_bb_4.description: From a hang, fold your entire body and touch your toes to the bar — complete hip-flexor strength, grip, and body-control in one movement.

core_hf_1.title: Hanging Windshield Wipers
core_hf_1.description: Hang from the bar, raise legs to horizontal and sweep them side to side. Builds the lateral core strength and hip mobility needed for the human flag.

core_hf_2.title: Tucked Human Flag
core_hf_2.description: Grip a vertical pole and hold your body horizontal with knees tucked — the first true human flag position requiring elite lateral force production.

core_hf_3.title: One-Leg Human Flag
core_hf_3.description: One leg extended, one leg bent — a transitional hold that dramatically reduces lever arm while training the lateral chain for the full flag.

core_hf_4.title: Human Flag
core_hf_4.description: Grip a vertical pole and hold your entire body horizontal — a legendary feat demanding elite lateral core and shoulder strength.

core_weighted_1.title: Weighted Plank
core_weighted_1.description: Hold a rigid plank with weight plates or a vest on your back. The added load magnifies the anti-extension demand, making this the most direct path to elite core stiffness under load.

core_weighted_2.title: Weighted Leg Raises
core_weighted_2.description: Hang from the bar wearing ankle weights and raise straight legs to horizontal. The added load dramatically increases hip-flexor demand and grip endurance requirements.

core_weighted_3.title: Weighted Dragon Flag
core_weighted_3.description: Perform the Dragon Flag with a weight vest — one of the most brutal loaded bodyweight core exercises in existence. Total anti-extension strength under external load.

core_rings_1.title: Ring Knee Raises
core_rings_1.description: Hang from gymnastic rings and drive your knees to your chest. The instability forces deep shoulder packing and superior core compression compared to a fixed bar.

core_rings_2.title: Ring Rollouts
core_rings_2.description: From kneeling, grip gymnastic rings and roll out to full extension. The constant instability forces the deep stabilisers to work overtime — harder than any barbell or roller equivalent.

core_roller_1.title: Ab Roller Rollout
core_roller_1.description: Grip the ab roller and roll from kneeling to full extension, keeping hips locked. The explosive anti-extension demand and full range of motion makes this one of the most effective loaded core movements available.

core_band_1.title: Banded Pallof Press
core_band_1.description: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and press the handle directly away from your body while resisting rotation. The anti-rotation demand targets deep spinal stabilisers that no crunching movement can access.

legs_1.title: Squat Foundation
legs_1.description: Build the bilateral squat pattern with full depth and upright posture.

legs_2.title: Squat Strength
legs_2.description: Increase squat volume and dial in knee tracking and depth. Unlocks the L-Sit and Pistol Squat paths.

legs_3.title: Shrimp Squat
legs_3.description: Single-leg squat with the rear foot held behind you — demands exceptional quad strength, ankle mobility and balance simultaneously.

legs_4.title: Bulgarian Split Squat
legs_4.description: Rear foot elevated, front foot forward — sink until the rear knee grazes the floor. One of the most effective unilateral strength builders.

legs_ls_1.title: Pike Stretch
legs_ls_1.description: Sit tall with legs straight and fold forward over them — builds the hamstring flexibility and hip-flexor activation needed for a full L-sit.

legs_ls_2.title: L-Sit Compressions
legs_ls_2.description: Seated, drive your heels into the floor and try to lift them — builds the active hip-flexor compression that replaces flexibility with strength in the L-sit.

legs_ls_3.title: Tuck L-Sit
legs_ls_3.description: Press on parallel bars or the floor and lift your hips clear — knees tucked to chest, arms locked out. The gateway position for the full L-sit.

legs_ls_4.title: Full L-Sit
legs_ls_4.description: Arms locked, hips lifted, legs straight and horizontal — a complete display of hip-flexor strength, pressing power and body compression.

legs_ps_1.title: Step-Ups
legs_ps_1.description: Step onto an elevated surface under control — develops single-leg stability and quad activation as the first step toward the pistol squat.

legs_ps_2.title: Assisted Pistol Squat
legs_ps_2.description: Full-depth single-leg squat holding a counterbalance or support — builds the strength and mobility pattern before removing assistance.

legs_ps_3.title: Close-Stance Squat
legs_ps_3.description: Bilateral squat with feet together — approximates pistol squat mechanics and ankle mobility demands before going fully unilateral.

legs_ps_4.title: Pistol Squat
legs_ps_4.description: Full-depth single-leg squat with the free leg extended — demands quad strength, ankle mobility and total-body balance in one elite movement.

legs_weighted_1.title: Weighted Goblet Squat
legs_weighted_1.description: Hold a kettlebell or dumbbell at chest height and squat to depth. The goblet position promotes vertical torso and deep knee tracking, making it the ideal loaded entry point for leg strength.

legs_weighted_2.title: Weighted Bulgarian Split Squat
legs_weighted_2.description: Hold dumbbells and perform a rear-foot elevated split squat. Unilateral loading under this degree of hip-flexor stretch is one of the most effective strength builders for the legs.

legs_weighted_3.title: Weighted Pistol Squat
legs_weighted_3.description: Perform the full pistol squat holding a kettlebell or weight plate. Adding load to this already-demanding movement requires exceptional ankle mobility, single-leg strength, and balance.

legs_weighted_4.title: Weighted Shrimp Squat
legs_weighted_4.description: Perform the shrimp squat with a weight vest or dumbbells — one of the most advanced loaded unilateral movements. Demands elite hip flexor, quad, and balance under external resistance.

legs_band_1.title: Banded Lateral Walks
legs_band_1.description: Place a resistance band around your ankles and walk laterally in a quarter-squat position. Targets the gluteus medius and hip abductors that stabilise every single-leg movement.

legs_box_1.title: Box Jumps
legs_box_1.description: Explode off the ground and land softly on a plyo box, absorbing the impact through a controlled cushioned landing. Introduces rate of force development and elastic energy storage.

legs_sliders_1.title: Slider Hamstring Curls
legs_sliders_1.description: Lie on your back, place sliders under your heels, and curl your legs toward your glutes while keeping your hips bridged. The high eccentric demand creates stimulus that machines cannot replicate.

push_rings_1.title: Ring Dip
push_rings_1.description: Dip on gymnastic rings with controlled RTO (Rings Turned Out) at lockout. The instability demands elite tricep, chest, and shoulder stabilisation on every rep.

push_rings_2.title: Ring Muscle-Up
push_rings_2.description: Combine ring pulling and pressing power in a single explosive movement above the rings. The ultimate ring skill requires elite stability across the entire kinetic chain.

push_weighted_1.title: Weighted Dip
push_weighted_1.description: Add a vest or belt and dip under load. Weighted dips build elite pressing strength faster than any other bodyweight compound movement.
